name: Maximize eight-suite utilization and data throughput
consequences: Maximizing eight-suite capacity boosts data throughput and reduces per-participant time to event capture, but adds scheduling and annotation bottlenecks if reviewer cadence does not scale. The approach also introduces potential staff workload intensification that could affect data quality if not managed carefully.
options: Optimize participant scheduling and night-shift deployment to sustain eight active suites while maintaining safety margins and data quality, aiming for a stable baseline annotation rate.
Develop a dynamic throughput model prioritizing higher-yield participant profiles to maximize event capture within existing capacity, slowing expansion until metrics stabilize.
Pilot a modular annex with temporary installations and rapid safety certification to reach twelve suites in peak periods if early data justify it.
review: Trade-off: maximizing eight-suite capacity boosts data throughput, but adds scheduling and annotation bottlenecks if reviewer cadence does not scale, leaving a gap in explicit throughput targets and staffing adequacy.

name: Controlled de-identification and external data sharing framework
consequences: Strengthened privacy controls reduce external validation opportunities and the ability to benchmark across sites, potentially limiting reproducibility. The governance overhead may slow responsive data sharing and complicate cross-institution collaborations.
options: Publish de-identified physiological dataset through a tiered access model with institutional data use agreements and an oversight committee.
Limit public releases to aggregated statistics and ensure all video remains non-deposited, enforcing privacy walls and audit trails.
Pilot a secure data enclave with controlled remote access and strict versioning, establishing governance before any external collaboration.
review: Trade-off: tighter privacy controls reduce opportunities for external validation and multi-site benchmarking, and the three options still constrain public data access while requiring ongoing governance overhead.

name: Semi-automated event-triage tool development
consequences: Automation aims to accelerate adjudication and standardize scoring, but can introduce model bias and overfitting to local data. The three options inherently leave gaps in external validation and governance oversight.
options: Implement a semi-automated triage workflow surfacing probable parasomnia episodes for two-scored human adjudications and iteratively retraining on disagreement data.
Adopt a transfer-learning approach, reusing a validated model from related neurophysiology data with domain-specific fine-tuning and cross-site validation.
Create a secure, cloud-based scoring environment with concurrent multi-scorer review and explicit audit trails to accelerate adjudication while maintaining data security.
review: Trade-off: automation accelerates adjudication but risks introducing model bias and overfitting to local data; the three options still leave gaps in external validation and governance oversight.

name: Night shift staffing architecture for safety and throughput
consequences: Steady night staffing enhances safety and coverage, but raises ongoing personnel costs and administrative burden. The options leave gaps in long-term cost control and resilience during staff shortages.
options: Maintain rotating night shifts with cross-trained technicians and a dedicated on-call supervisor to ensure rapid response and continuous coverage across eight active suites.
Create a dedicated on-site clinical psychologist presence during peak nights to monitor distress, support consent processes, and maintain ethical standards.
Contract a flexible external staffing pool to cover surges, balancing costs with margins while ensuring German social insurance compliance.
review: Trade-off: steady night staffing enhances safety and coverage, but raises ongoing personnel costs; the options leave gaps in long-term cost control and resilience during staff shortages.

name: Participant recruitment funnel optimization and inclusion criteria
consequences: Expands recruitment reach and accelerates enrollment, but may introduce greater heterogeneity in baseline characteristics and increase screening workload. The options may also raise challenges in maintaining data comparability across cohorts.
options: Expand recruitment channels to regional sleep clinics and hospitals with streamlined pre-admission pathways to sustain target enrollment.
Broaden eligibility to include complementary parasomnia presentations with careful safety monitoring to maintain representativeness while preserving study integrity.
Implement staged consent and pre-screening protocols to accelerate eligibility confirmation and reduce screen-out rates across sites.
review: Trade-off: broader recruitment improves sample size and timeline but risks heterogeneous data and variable event yield; the options leave gaps in standardizing pre-screening quality and ensuring consistent baseline comparability.

name: Data stewardship and consent architecture
consequences: Stronger governance reduces risk and builds trust with participants and funders, but may slow external validation and reuse. The three options leave gaps in scalable sharing workflows and clear governance metrics.
options: Adopt a tiered consent model with participant preferences for data sharing levels and robust data-use contracts across collaborations.
Proceed with on-site storage and encrypted backups while minimizing cross-institutional data transfer to reduce breach risk.
Negotiate a standing data-sharing agreement with the university library for long-term storage and public de-identified datasets after a defined threshold.
review: Trade-off: stronger data governance reduces risk and builds trust, but slows external validation and reuse; the options leave gaps in scalable sharing workflows and clear governance metrics.

name: Phase-gated monitoring tiering and escalation protocol
consequences: Phase-gated monitoring increases data richness during enhanced nights but raises staffing and coordination costs; the approach also adds scheduling complexity that can reduce throughput if not carefully managed. The downstream implication is a potential bottleneck in nightly coverage, especially during high-activity periods, which may require adaptive staffing and clear escalation criteria.
options: Implement a strict three-tier nightly schedule where baseline nights rely on dry-electrode EEG and mattress sensors, enhanced nights add full PSG components, and escalation nights trigger clinician review.

Pilot a rolling phase cadence where participants’ stays are extended only after sufficient events are captured, ensuring data density before escalation but potentially lengthening recruitment timelines.

Set algorithmic escalation triggers that prompt targeted PSG when event probability crosses predefined thresholds, reducing unnecessary full-night monitoring while preserving clinical sensitivity and limiting false positives.
review: Phase-gated monitoring increases data richness but raises staffing and coordination costs; the three options leave unaddressed how to sustain throughput if event density remains low.

name: Privacy-preserving data governance and access controls
consequences: Establishing privacy safeguards enables external validation without compromising participant privacy, but may slow data-sharing cycles. The downstream implication is potential delays in replication efforts or external collaborations unless data-use agreements and governance processes are streamlined.
options: Establish role-based access controls and formal data-use agreements for de-identified sensor data to enable external collaborations while preserving participant privacy.
Create a two-tier data-release workflow where basic sensor data are published in restricted repositories after internal validation, preserving privacy and auditability.
Implement a dynamic consent mechanism that clarifies permissible data sharing levels, requiring re-consent for new data types or partner collaborations.
review: Privacy governance enables external validation while preserving privacy, but may slow data-sharing cycles; the three options leave unaddressed how to balance rapid replication with evolving consent requirements and auditability.

name: Residential environment safety and naturalism balance
consequences: Investments in safety features improve participant safety and acceptance of the domestic setting; however, heightened safety could dampen naturalistic behavior or increase complaints if intrusiveness is perceived. The downstream implication is a need for ongoing design iterations and participant feedback integration.
options: Develop a safety-first design guide that prioritizes padded edges and restricted openings while preserving familiar home-like aesthetics to minimize behavioral suppression.
Pilot flexible alarm systems that trigger only when risk thresholds are exceeded, reducing unnecessary alerts yet maintaining rapid response capability.
Implement continuous safety audits and participant feedback loops to iteratively adjust layout and signaling, balancing comfort with vigilance.
review: Residential safety balance improves participant trust and protocol fidelity, but could impede naturalistic behavior; the three options leave unaddressed how to quantify the acceptable level of intrusiveness without compromising safety.

name: Dual-scorer reliability and scoring workflow optimization
consequences: Enhanced scoring reliability reduces misclassification and increases data integrity; however, it doubles scorer workload and can slow data turnaround, impacting timely analysis and publication cycles.
options: Establish independent scoring with two blinded raters per night and a reconciliation step to resolve discrepancies, ensuring higher annotation fidelity.
Implement a scoring-automation-augmented review where a predefined consensus protocol guides when human adjudication is needed.
Institute quarterly cross-checks with external sleep-annotation experts to benchmark intra-rater reliability and identify systematic biases.
review: Dual-scorer reliability enhances annotation quality but increases workload and turnaround time; the three options leave unaddressed how to mitigate bottlenecks if scorer availability is limited.

name: Adaptive recruitment cadence and pre-screening optimization
consequences: Tuning recruitment cadence helps meet enrollment targets while ensuring eligibility; however, shifting channels or criteria may impact study representativeness and screening overhead.
options: Implement a rolling recruitment framework that prioritizes the Bonn region and clinician referrals to sustain steady enrollment while maintaining eligibility.
Introduce structured collateral review and partner outreach to reduce screening fatigue, enabling efficient pre-screening and faster consent acquisition.
Experiment with staged inclusion criteria adjustments after interim data review to balance safety with enrollment pace and data yield.
review: Adaptive recruitment cadence aligns enrollment with study needs but may affect sample representativeness; the three options leave unaddressed how to prevent channel bias as recruitment channels shift.

name: Data quality assurance and annotation throughput optimization
consequences: Improved quality assurance ensures robust datasets and reduces rework; however, stricter QC gates may slow annotation throughput and prolong study timelines.
options: Institute a structured QC pipeline with predefined scoring rubrics and clocked review windows to stabilize annotation accuracy across raters.
Launch a targeted training curriculum for technicians and raters to shorten learning curve and improve consistency in event annotation.
Pilot a lightweight semi-automatic annotation tool that suggests labels for reviewer validation, preserving human oversight.
review: Data quality assurance improves robustness but could slow annotation throughput; the three options leave unaddressed whether initial strict QC will hinder timely analyses if data volume spikes.

name: Dynamic observation density zoning within suites
consequences: Increasing observation density on selected nights improves the likelihood of capturing parasomnia events and enriches the dataset. A downstream implication is higher participant fatigue and greater scheduling complexity for staff, which can reduce overall stay comfort and safety if not managed.
options: Reallocate high-sensitivity PSG nights to the weeks with elevated event likelihood based on interim checks, maximizing data yield while reducing participant fatigue.
Cluster enhanced-night PSG sessions to participants with higher prior event history identified through pre-admission screening to concentrate resources on likely events.
Implement a flexible scheduling framework that rotates enhanced nights across participants to balance data collection with staff workload and safety considerations.
review: Trade-off is data concentration versus participant burden; the three options leave unaddressed whether long-term fatigue affects recruitment or whether seasonality undermines generalizability.

name: Seasonal recruitment channel diversification
consequences: Diversifying recruitment channels broadens participant reach and reduces dependence on a single network. A downstream trade-off is increased coordination overhead and potential variability in screening rigor across sites.
options: Expand engagement with regional clinics, sleep societies, and neurology networks to drive staggered referrals across enrollment windows and reduce single-source dependency.
Implement structured pre-screening tele-assessments to identify likely candidates before in-person visits, conserving clinic time and resources.
Offer flexible consent pathways and transportation support to increase participation among hard-to-reach populations while maintaining ethical compliance.
review: Trade-off is broader enrollment reach versus increased coordination complexity; options leave unaddressed whether screening quality remains consistent across channels, potentially affecting data comparability.

name: External data stream fusion for anomaly prioritization
consequences: Cross-validating multiple streams improves triage accuracy and can reduce manual review workload. A downstream implication is potential integration latency and added governance overhead, which may delay decision-making if not optimized.
options: Develop a rules-based fusion layer that cross-validates dry-electrode, mattress, camera, and ambient data to highlight probable events for rapid reviewer triage.
Pilot a lightweight multi-stream weighting approach that favors streams with historically higher reliability without asserting autonomous detection.
Engage a secure analytics partner to manage data bursts during peak capture periods while preserving de-identification and access controls.
review: Trade-off is integration complexity and potential latency; options leave unaddressed how to preserve auditability when fusion results guide scorer decisions.

name: Modular expansion gating based on pilot data quality
consequences: Gated expansion reduces capital risk by aligning scale with demonstrated data quality. Downstream, gating can delay growth and slow achievement of study milestones if targets are difficult to reach.
options: Define milestone-driven expansion triggers tied to data quality, consent rates, and event yield to unlock additional suites only after meeting targets.
Pilot two additional suites during a 6–week pilot phase with shared staffing to validate operational efficiency before committing permanent renovations.
Institute a real-time data quality dashboard and governance reviews on a weekly cadence to inform scalable investments.
review: Trade-off is speed of scale versus confidence in data quality; options leave unaddressed whether external audits are needed to validate rolling metrics.

name: Enhanced privacy-preserving annotation governance
consequences: Strengthening governance improves consent integrity and reduces risk of data leakage. It may slow scoring throughput and require additional training and oversight.
options: Adopt an offline annotation workflow where two independent scorers review de-identified data before any data release, with strict access controls.
Implement cryptographic auditing and access-control logs to verify scorer reliability without exposing sensitive identifiers.
Schedule quarterly privacy compliance workshops and refreshers to reinforce bedroom video constraints and consent scope during all study phases.
review: Trade-off is throughput versus privacy rigor; options leave unaddressed whether external collaborators can participate under governance while maintaining strict controls.

name: Incentive-aligned participant retention and compliance strategy
consequences: Higher retention improves data completeness and reduces re-screening burden. But it increases budget pressure and may bias the sample toward participants who value compensation.
options: Design a participant engagement program with regular check-ins and transparent progress updates to minimize dropout during long stays.
Offer milestone-based compensation tied to completed nights and scoring rounds to maintain motivation while preserving ethical boundaries.
Provide transportation subsidies and lodging flexibility to accommodate personal obligations and reduce missed nights.
review: Trade-off is cost pressure versus data completeness; options leave unaddressed whether compensation structure biases enrollment toward specific demographics.
